Compute eventual ejection probabilities given platform dynamics.
Let p1, p2, p3 be probabilities a ball is eventually ejected when it is currently in positions 1, 2, 3.
• If in position1: piston1 ejects it (prob 1/3); pistons2 or3 release it.  p1 = 1/3.
• If in position2: piston2 ejects (1/3); pistons1 or3 move it to pos1.  p2 = 1/3 + (2/3)p1 = 5/9.
• If in position3: piston3 ejects (1/3); piston2 moves it to pos1, piston1 moves it to pos2.  p3 = 1/3 + (1/3)p1 + (1/3)p2 = 17/27 ≈ 0.63.
Initial positions: ball1 starts in pos1 → 1/3; ball2 pos2 → 5/9; ball3 pos3 → 17/27.
For balls 4–100, entry position distribution: 40% to pos2, 60% to pos3 (steady-state). Their ejection probability = 0.4·p2 + 0.6·p3 = 3/5 = 0.6 < 17/27.
Therefore ball3 has the highest chance of being ejected.

At the instant the pistons start, Ball 3 is sitting in position 3.  A ball that enters position 3 is ejected with probability
E3 = 17⁄27 ≈ 0.62963.

Ball 1 starts in position 1 and can win only if piston 1 fires immediately, so its chance is 1⁄3.
Ball 2 starts in position 2, giving it an eventual ejection probability of 5⁄9 ≈ 0.55556.

For every later ball n ≥ 4 the ejection probability oscillates about 0.6 with a decaying amplitude:
P(win for ball n) = 0.6 ± 0.01975·(2⁄3)^{n-4},
so it never exceeds Ball 3’s 17⁄27 ≈ 0.62963.

Therefore the highest winning probability belongs to Ball 3.
